subject.title: fix(config): reject zero-value pruneAfter to prevent silent data loss

question: Should the zero-duration rejection and doctor-removal migration land after the branch is refreshed and lint is green, accepting that affected existing configs require doctor repair during upgrade?
rationale: The implementation follows repository migration policy and prevents data loss, but deliberately turns a previously accepted configuration into an upgrade-visible validation failure until repaired.

options.title: Refresh, verify, and merge
options.body: Rebase or update the branch, confirm the doctor repair against existing string and numeric zero configs, require green lint and focused tests, then merge the safety fix.

options.title: Pause for another upgrade design
options.body: Hold the PR only if maintainers want a different migration or automatic upgrade experience rather than the established doctor-fix path.

recommendation.title: Refresh, verify, and merge
recommendation.body: Rebase or update the branch, confirm the doctor repair against existing string and numeric zero configs, require green lint and focused tests, then merge the safety fix.
